assessment: T4P140 compares oral safflower oil with fish oil in inactive adults with abdominal obesity and measures fasting lipids and lipoproteins. Pressing method and gait were unreported. A distinct walking study compares chewing gum with powder, without safflower as the causal contrast.

PP0024 summarizes peppermint–caraway oil as a combined short-term treatment for functional dyspepsia. The cited outcomes are gastrointestinal symptoms, and the contribution of ground caraway to fatigue was not studied.

BASIL labels the Better Assessment of Illness delirium study, and Basil Eldadah is a symposium discussant. The separate hyposmia presentation measures odor identification and neuroimaging in community-dwelling older adults. None evaluates fresh basil consumption.

The culinary education presentation measures medical students' intention to eat more lentils or beans after a course. A separate Parkinson-related back-pain vignette discusses rigidity and use of dopaminergic medication and rehabilitation. Neither tests boiled lentils for rigidity.
